4. In Civil Revision No.1128 of 1993 the petitioner filed Money Suit No. 5 of 1983 in which compromise decree was passed on 24-2-84 and since the opposite parties failed to pay the decretal dues the petitioner at first filed Money Execution Case No. 1 of 1985 in which. 0.71/2 acre of land situated in khatian No.563, as shown in column 2(a) of the Form of Money Execution Case No. 5 of 1988, was sold in auction on 25-8-87 for Taka 55,000 and subsequently, the petitioner having failed to trace out any other properties of the opposite parties filed Execution Case No. 11 of 1990 on 8-9-90 for realisation of the balance decretal dues of Taka 8,04, 717.13 along with the interest of Taka 15,041.50 by way of civil imprisonment of the opposite parties. 

 5. In Civil Revision No. 1129 of 1993 the petitioner filed Money Execution Case No. 6 of 1984 in which compromise decree was passed on 14-2-84 and since the opposite parties failed to pay the decretal dues the petitioner filed Money Execution case No. 2 of 1985 in which 0.99 acres of land, out of 1.19 acres of SA Dag No. 28 in Khatian No.190, which has also been shown in column 2(a) of the Form of Execution Case No. 5 of 1988, was sold in auction on 25-8-87 for Taka 35,000 subsequently, the petitioner having failed to trace out any other properties for the opposite parties filed Money Execution Case No.12 of 1990 praying for realisation of the balance amount of Taka 786267.86 along with cost of Taka 1458950 by way of civil imprisonment of the opposite parties. Thereafter, in both Money Execution Case Nos. 11 and 12 of 1990 the learned Subordinate Judge passed the impugned orders rejecting the aforesaid money execution cases on the ground that in their affidavit the petitioner admitted that they hold second charge on the moveable and immoveable properties of Kalaroa Ice and Cold Storage Ltd and that the opposite parties also expressed their intention to repay the decretal dues by operating the cold storage and that opposite parties admittedly have no other properties and that the opposite party Nos. 4 and 5 are minors and opposite party No.2 is a woman and so it will also not be proper to put them in civil imprisonment for realisation of the dues of the petitioner.
